items.note: In all three samples the hovered first product card lifts up and to the left as one outlined box, with a hard ink offset shadow at its lower right. The yellow band above has ink text and quiet pills, the grid stays unchanged, and nothing overlaps.

In dark mode the hovered card lifts the same way, with a light 35% offset shadow on the black ground. Card bodies are raised dark gray, price tags stay pink, and the selected 'All' pill is the inverse fill.

At phone width the cards stack in one column and the first card shows the lift and offset shadow. The band collapses to the title, subtitle and a pill strip that scrolls sideways, as the layout rules ask.

After adding to cart, a raised toast with an ink border and hard shadow sits at the bottom left. It has a check icon, the message 'Added 1 item … to your cart', a 'View cart' link and a close button, and the cart count in the header changes to 1. The single pink action is 'Add to cart', which stays lifted.
In dark mode the toast is a dark raised card with a light offset shadow and a clear message and link. The yellow band title stays ink-on-yellow, and the paper-filled cart button shows the count of 1.

On mobile the toast is pinned to the bottom edge across the width, with the message, the 'View cart' link and a close button. The product sticker, the pink price tag, the outlined color pills and the stepper all read cleanly above it.

The 'Your cart' band (a blue band in two samples, teal in one) sits over two outlined cards. In the checkout card, each empty field has a red border and an icon-plus-sentence message under it, and a summary line asks to fix the 3 fields. The first field has the focus ring, and 'Place order' is the one pink action.

In dark mode the same error layout holds: red-bordered inputs on raised dark cards, readable messages with an icon (not color alone), a pink halo on the focused field and a single pink 'Place order' button.

On mobile the form is one column under the items card. The error summary, the per-field messages with icons, and the ring on the focused 'Full name' field are all visible, and 'Place order' stays in the flow rather than in a fixed bar.
The keyboard focus lands on the header 'Cart' link and shows a visible ring next to the ink current-page 'Shop' pill. The rest of the shop grid stays at rest with flat outlined cards.
In dark mode the focused 'Cart' link carries a pink ring, clearly visible against the dark header, next to the paper-filled 'Shop' pill. The cards and band are unchanged.
At phone width the focus ring shows on the 'Cart' link in the second header row, beside the ink 'Shop' pill, above the collapsed yellow band and the single-column card list.

Each sample has eleven distinct flat sticker objects on band-color squares: tote, backpack, duffel, sweater, tee, jacket, mug, skillet, towels, key ring and beanie. Each reads as its product. Fills come from pink, band colors and paper, with ink outlines. Sample 2's outlines are visibly thinner than the heavy outline the recipe asks for.

Each sample's detail image is a tilted tote sticker with an ink outline, a pink or paper body, a pocket or tag detail, and handles on a yellow band square. It reads instantly as a bag and matches the grid's drawing for the same item.
Each sample shows a tilted crew sweater with ribbed hem and cuffs, ink-outlined, in pink or blue on a contrasting band square. Sample 2 adds a yellow collar. All three read as knitwear.

The cart sticker is an open box with a plus in sample 1, and a pink coin with a yellow extruded rim and a plus glyph in samples 2 and 3. Both are flat, heavy-outlined and tilted, at the small sticker size for a dense screen.

findings.summary: In one sample, the product stickers are drawn with an outline of about 2px at their roughly 250px display size. The recipe asks for a heavy 4px ink outline at that size, so these stickers look lighter and more like line icons than the reference's bold sticker art. The other two samples hold the heavier weight.
